FAQ: Why did the same interaction score differently when re-scored?

FAQ ID: FAQ-005
Q: The same call was scored differently when re-evaluated. Why?
A:
This typically happens when scoring workers are using different rubric versions or cached rubric weights after a configuration rollout.
First verify the active rubric version, then run the “QM Rubric Cache Reset + Re-score” recovery steps.
If the issue persists, escalate to platform on-call because the rollout may be incomplete.

================================================================================
KNOWN ISSUE — KI-2025-002
Copilot Suggestions Delayed > 10 Seconds
================================================================================

Issue ID     : KI-2025-002
Severity     : P2
Status       : Workaround Available
Reported     : October 22, 2025
Affected     : 2025 Wave 2

SYMPTOMS:
---------
1. Agent opens a conversation and Copilot panel loads
2. Copilot shows spinning indicator for 10-30 seconds
3. Sometimes Copilot request times out completely
4. Most frequent during peak hours (9 AM - 12 PM local time)
5. Non-peak hours: Copilot responds in expected 2-3 seconds

ROOT CAUSE:
-----------
Azure OpenAI Service throttling when tenant exceeds the configured
Tokens Per Minute (TPM) quota. The default quota for most tenants is
120K TPM. During peak hours, concurrent Copilot requests from multiple
agents can exceed this limit, causing queuing and timeouts.

Each Copilot request consumes approximately:
- Case summarization: ~2,000 tokens
- Response suggestion: ~1,500 tokens
- Knowledge recommendation: ~1,000 tokens

With 200 agents active, each generating ~3 requests/min:

IMPACT:

Option 2: Enable Copilot Response Caching
  1. Admin center > Productivity > Copilot > Settings
  2. Enable "Cache frequent suggestions"
  3. Cache TTL: 15 minutes (default)
  4. Reduces unique Azure OpenAI calls by ~40%

Option 3: Stagger Copilot Features
  - Disable less critical features during peak:

    3. Disable temporarily: Response suggestions, Knowledge recommendations
  - Re-enable during off-peak

MONITORING:
-----------
Check Azure OpenAI usage:
  Azure Portal > Azure OpenAI resource > Metrics
  - Metric: "Tokens per minute" (TPM) used vs. quota
  - Metric: "HTTP 429 responses" (throttling events)
  - Set alert: When 429 count > 10 in 5-minute window

Check Copilot latency in Application Insights:
  requests

  | summarize avg_duration_ms = avg(duration), p95 = percentile(duration, 95)
      by bin(timestamp, 5m)
  | render timechart

Known Issue: QM scorecards show inconsistent results across runs

Issue ID: KI-005
Severity: P2
Status: Workaround Available
Affected Versions: 2025 Wave 2

Symptoms:
- The same call is scored differently when re-evaluated (±15–25 points).
- Coaching recommendations flip between “Needs Improvement” and “Meets Expectations”.
- Supervisors report sudden spikes in “policy violation” tags with no process change.

Root Cause (hypothesis):
A scoring model version mismatch: some jobs still use the previous rubric weights after a background configuration rollout.
Cached rubric weights are not invalidated for long-running evaluation workers.

Workaround:
- Force-refresh rubric configuration and clear QM scoring cache.
- Re-run scoring in “strict rubric mode” for impacted queues until rollout completes.

Operational Notes:
- Check recent config deployments for QM rubric/weights changes.
- Validate that all workers are on the same scoring configuration version.

KNOWN ISSUE — KI-2025-003
Chat Widget Not Loading on Safari
================================================================================

Issue ID     : KI-2025-003
Severity     : P2
Status       : Workaround Available
Reported     : October 30, 2025
Affected     : 2025 Wave 2

SYMPTOMS:
---------
1. Live chat widget fails to render on Safari 17+
2. Browser console shows "SecurityError: Blocked a frame with origin..."
3. Widget iframe loads but session cookie is rejected
4. Affects both macOS Safari and iOS Safari
5. Works correctly on Chrome, Edge, and Firefox

ROOT CAUSE:
-----------
Safari's Intelligent Tracking Prevention (ITP) blocks third-party cookies
by default. The CCaaS chat widget runs in an iframe from a Microsoft domain
(*.omnichannelengagementhub.com), which Safari treats as a third-party
context. The session authentication cookie is blocked, preventing the
widget from establishing a chat

IMPACT:
-------
- All customers using Safari (approx. 15% of web traffic) cannot use live chat

- Customers see an empty chat panel or "Chat unavailable" message

WORKAROUND:
-----------
Recommended Fix: Enable First-Party Cookie Mode

1. In admin center > Channels > Chat > Widget settings
2. Find "Cookie configuration" section
3. Set cookieDomain to the customer's own domain:
   Example: If customer website is www.contoso.com
   Set cookieDomain = "contoso.com"

4. Update the chat widget JavaScript snippet:

   <script>
     Microsoft.Omnichannel.LiveChatWidget.SDK.setContextProvider({
       cookieDomain: "contoso.com",
       usePrimaryDomainCookies: true
     });
   </script>

This forces the widget to use first-party cookies under the customer's
